Key Finding: Participation in online collaborative consumption is motivated by sustainability, enjoyment, and economic gains, yet positive attitudes toward sharing do not always translate into actual participation.
APA Reference: Hamari, J., Sjöklint, M., & Ukkonen, A. (2016). The sharing economy: Why people participate in collaborative consumption. Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology, 67(9), 2047–2059. https://doi.org/10.1002/asi.23552

Key Finding: Sharing is ancient, while internet-based collaborative consumption and the sharing economy are newer phenomena that are both growing in popularity and challenge the idea that identity depends on ownership.
APA Reference: Belk, R. (2014). You are what you can access: Sharing and collaborative consumption online. Journal of Business Research, 67(8), 1595–1600. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbusres.2013.10.001

Key Finding: A meta-analysis of 128 experiments found that tangible rewards and engagement-contingent rewards significantly undermined people's free-choice intrinsic motivation.
APA Reference: Deci, E. L., Koestner, R., & Ryan, R. M. (1999). A meta-analytic review of experiments examining the effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation. Psychological Bulletin, 125(6), 627–668. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.125.6.627

Key Finding: In mobility data covering 1.5 million people, a few outside location points were enough to uniquely identify most individuals, and coarsening location or time resolution offered little anonymity.
APA Reference: de Montjoye, Y.-A., Hidalgo, C. A., Verleysen, M., & Blondel, V. D. (2013). Unique in the crowd: The privacy bounds of human mobility. Scientific Reports, 3, Article 1376. https://doi.org/10.1038/srep01376

Key Finding: A literature survey of computational location privacy reviews attitudes toward location privacy, computational threats from leaked location data, and countermeasures such as anonymity and obfuscation.
APA Reference: Krumm, J. (2009). A survey of computational location privacy. Personal and Ubiquitous Computing, 13(6), 391–399. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00779-008-0212-5

Key Finding: Web 2.0, geotags, GPS, and broadband let ordinary volunteers create geographic information, raising open questions about the accuracy of the results and the threat to individual privacy.
APA Reference: Goodchild, M. F. (2007). Citizens as sensors: The world of volunteered geography. GeoJournal, 69(4), 211–221. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10708-007-9111-y

Key Finding: The sharing economy challenges marketing's traditional foundations, including institutions such as consumers, firms, channels, and regulators, and presents paradoxes tied to its maturation and technology.
APA Reference: Eckhardt, G. M., Houston, M. B., Jiang, B., Lamberton, C., Rindfleisch, A., & Zervas, G. (2019). Marketing in the sharing economy. Journal of Marketing, 83(5), 5–27. https://doi.org/10.1177/0022242919861929

Key Finding: The World Bank projects Philippine growth slowing to 3.7 percent in 2026 as a global energy price surge lifted inflation and weighed on consumption and jobs, with the heaviest burden on the poorest 30 percent of households.
APA Reference: World Bank. (2026). Philippines economic update, midyear 2026: Powering progress: Electricity, competitiveness, and growth pathways. https://www.worldbank.org/ph

Key Finding: Poverty incidence among Filipino families declined to 10.9 percent in 2023, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority's preliminary national estimate.
APA Reference: Philippine Statistics Authority. (2024, July 22). Percentage of Filipino families classified as poor declined to 10.9 percent in 2023. https://psa.gov.ph/statistics/poverty/node/1684064817

Key Finding: The world wasted about 1.05 billion tonnes of food in 2022, nearly one fifth of the food available to consumers, with households accounting for 631 million tonnes.
APA Reference: United Nations Environment Programme. (2024, March 27). World squanders over 1 billion meals a day – UN report [Press release]. https://www.unep.org/index.php/news-and-stories/press-release/world-squanders-over-1-billion-meals-day-un-report

Key Finding: A record 62 million tonnes of e-waste was generated in 2022, only 22.3 percent was documented as formally collected and recycled, and volumes are on track to reach 82 million tonnes by 2030.
APA Reference: International Telecommunication Union & United Nations Institute for Training and Research. (2024). The global e-waste monitor 2024. https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Environment/Pages/Publications/The-Global-E-waste-Monitor-2024.aspx

Key Finding: Annual global waste generation is expected to grow from 2.01 billion tons to 3.40 billion tons by 2050.
APA Reference: Kaza, S., Yao, L. C., Bhada-Tata, P., & Van Woerden, F. (2018). What a waste 2.0: A global snapshot of solid waste management to 2050. World Bank. https://doi.org/10.1596/978-1-4648-1329-0

Key Finding: The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act sets a national program of waste reduction, reuse, recycling, and recovery, and makes barangays responsible for segregating and collecting reusable waste.
APA Reference: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000, Rep. Act No. 9003 (2001). https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2001/ra_9003_2001.html

Key Finding: The Extended Producer Responsibility Act of 2022 amends the solid waste law to require large enterprises to recover plastic packaging waste and promotes circular-economy practices such as reuse and recycling.
APA Reference: Extended Producer Responsibility Act of 2022, Rep. Act No. 11898 (2022). https://ldr.senate.gov.ph/legislative-issuance/republic-act-no-11898

Key Finding: The Local Government Code of 1991 declares the barangay the basic political unit and the primary planning and implementing unit of government policies, plans, and programs in the community.
APA Reference: Local Government Code of 1991, Rep. Act No. 7160 (1991). https://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1991/ra_7160_1991.html

Key Finding: The Data Privacy Act of 2012 protects personal information in government and private-sector information and communications systems and created the National Privacy Commission to oversee compliance.
APA Reference: Data Privacy Act of 2012, Rep. Act No. 10173 (2012). https://privacy.gov.ph/data-privacy-act/

Key Finding: The National Privacy Commission's implementing rules for the Data Privacy Act set general data privacy principles that govern how personal data may be processed.
APA Reference: National Privacy Commission. (2016). Implementing rules and regulations of Republic Act No. 10173, known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012. https://privacy.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/IRR_RA-10173-as-amended.pdf

Key Finding: The Internet Transactions Act of 2023 regulates B2B and B2C online transactions and sets platform liability rules but excludes consumer-to-consumer transactions from coverage.
APA Reference: Internet Transactions Act of 2023, Rep. Act No. 11967 (2023). https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2023/ra_11967_2023.html

Key Finding: Privacy is better judged by contextual integrity, meaning information gathering and distribution must be appropriate to the norms of the specific context in which it occurs.
APA Reference: Nissenbaum, H. (2004). Privacy as contextual integrity. Washington Law Review, 79(1), 119–158. https://digitalcommons.law.uw.edu/wlr/vol79/iss1/10

Key Finding: A taxonomy of privacy was developed to identify privacy problems comprehensively and concretely and to guide the law toward a more coherent understanding of privacy.
APA Reference: Solove, D. J. (2006). A taxonomy of privacy. University of Pennsylvania Law Review, 154(3), 477–564. https://doi.org/10.2307/40041279

Key Finding: Automated content moderation can increase opacity, complicate fairness and justice, and obscure the political nature of speech decisions, even when the systems are well optimized.
APA Reference: Gorwa, R., Binns, R., & Katzenbach, C. (2020). Algorithmic content moderation: Technical and political challenges in the automation of platform governance. Big Data & Society, 7(1), 1–15. https://doi.org/10.1177/2053951719897945
